newsitem.title: USA: Chip stocks rally amid signs of continued growth.
newsitem.headline: Chip stocks rally amid signs of continued growth.

text.p: Semiconductor stocks rallied Tuesday amid better-than-expected earnings and confirmation that the industry is recovering from last year's slump, analysts said.
The Philadelphia Stock Exchange semiconductor index gained 3.72 points or 1.27 percent to 295.53. Micron Technology Inc lead the gains among the chips makers, increasing 1-1/2 to 43-1/4.
Advanced Micro Devices Inc and Motorola Inc reported surprisingly strong earnings after the market closed Monday, fueling Tuesday's chip rally, analysts said.

Advanced Micro gained 1-5/8 to 42-7/8. Motorola, which had traded higher in advance of the earnings release, jumped higher Tuesday morning, but slipped throughout the day to 59-1/8, down 1-1/8. Despite the strong quarterly results, some investors viewed Motorola's industry growth forecast as positive, but cautious, analysts said.

Advanced Micro posted an unexpected first quarter profit of $0.09 a share, above Wall Street's consensus estimate of a loss of $0.03 a share. Advanced Micro's earnings bolstered hopes for equally strong results from other chip companies, analysts said.
"If a tertiary company like AMD can post strong numbers, it lends strength to the hope that the majors will," said Brian Eisenbarth, an analyst with Collins & Co.
"The fact that AMD is benefitting from chip demand reflects good underlying demand throughout the industry," said Robert Toomey, an analyst with Piper Jaffrey.

Motorola also surpassed Wall Street estimates, posting first quarter earnings of $0.53 a share, which included gains, versus $0.63 last year. Analysts had expected $0.45 a share, according to First Call.

Motorola called the recovery in the industry and its own chip business "very gradual." The company also said it expects the worldwide semiconductor industry to grow by about 10 percent in 1997, a forecast that some viewed as conservative.

Vadim Zlotnikov, an analyst with Sanford Bernstein said he expects semiconductor industry to grow about 13 percent in 1997, exceeding Motorola's forecast. He also expects personal computer growth to reach about 17 percent this year. He said prices of dynamic random access memory chips (DRAM) still remain a wild card, he said.
Chip order growth has increased as as networking companies and personal computer makers begin to replenish their inventories, Zlotnikov said.
"The recovery is in place. It will be gradual, based on continued strong demand," Toomey said.
Other chip stocks also rose Tuesday.
Teradyne Inc, which makes test and connection systems for semiconductor and telecommunications companies, also rallied, adding 2-1/2 to 35-7/8.
Texas Instruments Inc gained 1-1/8 to 86-5/8, National Semiconductor Corp increased 1/2 to 29-3/8 and Intel Corp firmed slightly, up 1/8 to 145-1/8.
